# Dashboard run comparison view (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

This epic delivers the run comparison capability in the RHOAI Dashboard: users
can select two or more training or pipeline runs and view their parameters and
metrics side by side, with a diff presentation that highlights which parameters
and metrics changed between two selected runs. This replaces the current
workflow of exporting run data to spreadsheets for comparison.

## Scope

- Add multi-run selection from the runs list in the Dashboard (two or more runs).
- Build a comparison view that presents the parameters and metrics of all
  selected runs side by side.
- Provide a diff presentation mode within the comparison view that highlights
  which parameters and metrics differ between two selected runs.
- Retrieve run parameters and metrics for both training runs and pipeline runs
  through the components' existing interfaces (no changes to the Data Science
  Pipelines component are in scope for this epic; the Dashboard consumes its
  existing surfaces).
- Comparison is limited to runs within a single project and cluster, per the
  strategy's out-of-scope statement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two or more runs in a project, when the user selects them from the runs
  list, then the Dashboard opens a comparison view showing the parameters and
  metrics of every selected run side by side.
- Given two selected runs in the comparison view, when the user activates the
  diff presentation, then the view highlights which parameters and metrics
  changed between the two runs.
- The comparison view works for training runs and for pipeline runs, with
  parameters and metrics retrieved through the existing component interfaces
  (validation that the existing Data Science Pipelines surfaces suffice for
  comparison; any gap found is raised back to the strategy rather than worked
  around with component changes in this epic).
- Comparison is offered only for runs within the same project and cluster.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and
  metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- HLR-3 (P1): Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and
  metrics changed between two selected runs. (Consolidated with HLR-1: the diff
  view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run
  data; both are covered here at the higher priority.)

# Run lineage for registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: registered model versions
link back to the run (training or pipeline run) that produced them, and that
linkage is exposed so a comparison can be opened starting from the Model
Registry.

## Scope

- Enable a registered model version to record a reference to the run that
  produced it, using the registry's existing metadata extension point for
  structured properties on model versions.
- Expose the producing-run reference through the registry's API so other
  surfaces (such as the Dashboard) can resolve which run produced a given
  model version.
- Ensure the linkage works for versions produced by training runs and by
  pipeline runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version, when its producing run is recorded, then
  the version carries a resolvable reference to that run retrievable through
  the registry's API.
- The producing-run reference can be populated for versions produced by
  training runs and by pipeline runs.
- The linkage mechanism uses the registry's existing metadata extension point
  and does not require changes to the registry's core entity model.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. (This epic
  covers the registry-side lineage; the Dashboard-side entry point that opens
  the comparison from the registry view is covered separately by the Dashboard
  team.)

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry view

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry entry point to the run comparison
capability: from a registered model version's view in the Dashboard, a user can
open the run comparison for the run that produced that version, and compare it
against other runs.

## Scope

- Add an action on the registered model version view in the Dashboard's Model
  Registry section that opens the run comparison capability, pre-populated with
  the run linked to that version via the registry's run-lineage metadata.
- Allow the user to add further runs to the comparison once it is opened from
  the registry.
- The entry point relies on the run comparison view already delivered by the
  Dashboard comparison capability and on the version-to-run linkage already
  exposed by the Model Registry; this epic builds the connecting navigation
  only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version whose producing run is recorded in the
  registry, when the user opens the comparison action from that version's view,
  then the run comparison opens with the producing run selected.
- Given a comparison opened from the Model Registry, when the user adds one or
  more additional runs, then the comparison presents them side by side with the
  producing run, including the diff presentation of changed parameters and
  metrics.
- Given a registered model version with no producing run recorded, when the
  user views the version, then the comparison action is unavailable or explains
  the missing linkage (no broken navigation).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): Registered model versions link back to the run that produced
  them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. (This epic
  covers the Dashboard-side entry point; the registry-side lineage metadata is
  covered separately by the Model Registry team.)

# Document the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic delivers end-user documentation for the run comparison workflow:
how to compare training and pipeline runs side by side and read the diff
presentation, and how to open a comparison starting from a registered model
version in the Model Registry.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list: selecting two or more runs, reading the side-by-side parameters
  and metrics view, and using the diff presentation of changed parameters and
  metrics.
- New documentation topic(s) covering the comparison workflow starting from the
  Model Registry: the version-to-run linkage and opening a comparison from a
  registered model version.
- Screenshots and procedure steps that reflect the shipped user experience for
  both entry points.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation includes a procedure for comparing runs from the runs list
  (multi-run selection, side-by-side view, diff presentation), accurate against
  the implemented behavior.
- Documentation includes a procedure for opening a comparison from a registered
  model version in the Model Registry, accurate against the implemented
  behavior.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented comparison
  capability and registry lineage behavior (reviewed by the implementing
  teams) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs
  list and the registry.

### HLR consolidation: HLR-1 + HLR-3 (logged per Step 4)

The strategy states one capability twice in different words (the problem
statement notes requirements were consolidated from two customer councils with
overlapping wording kept): "select two or more runs and view their parameters
and metrics side by side" (HLR-1) and "a run diff view highlighting which
parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs" (HLR-3). The diff
view is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run
data, for the same component and team. They are ONE capability: both HLR ids
are covered by RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 at the higher priority (P0). They were NOT
split into separate epics by priority label — on a shared surface a P0/P1 pair
is redundant wording, not a deferral signal.

### Priority split applied: HLR-2 dashboard entry point

The Dashboard-side portion of HLR-2 (opening a comparison from the registry

is a distinct, deferrable feature with independent user value (registry-originated
comparison) that does not share the P0 runs-list UI surface, and because folding

lineage metadata, hence its two incoming edges.

Can the strategy deliver partial value without it?\n153\t2. **YES** → Split into:\n154\t   - **Tier 1**: Independent work (user-facing features OR risk-reduction spikes/validations)\n155\t   - **Tier 2**: Dependency-gated work (blocked by upstream epic)\n156\t3. **NO** → Linear dependencies; external dependency blocks all downstream\n157\t\n158\t## Step 6: Classify Epics\n159\t\n160\tFor each epic, determine:\n161\t\n162\t### Type (mandatory)\n163\t- **Implementation**: Produce an artifact (code, config, docs, manifests, pipelines, RFCs, upstream PRs)\n164\t- **Investigation**: Resolve uncertainty (answer a question or make a decision that other epics depend on)\n165\t\n166\t### Implementation Type (optional routing label)\n167\t\n168\t| Label | When to apply |\n169\t|-------|--------------|\n170\t| `docs-authoring` | Red Hat docs content process — specialized tooling |\n171\t| `konflux-onboarding` | Build pipeline onboarding — known-recipe |\n172\t| `license-validation` | License scanning for transitive dependencies |\n173\t| `repo-onboarding` | Midstream repo fork creation under opendatahub-io |\n174\t| _(absent/null)_ | General-purpose — read target repo, figure it out |\n175\t\n176\t### AI Implementability Signals\n177\t\n178\tScore signals so the pipeline can compute an AI-implementability classification deterministically. **Do not compute the total score or classification yourself.** Use the signal set that matches the epic `type` — Implementation and Investigation epics measure different things.\n179\t\n180\t#### Implementation epics → `ai_signals` (9 signals)\n181\t\n182\tEvaluate each as +1 (favorable), 0 (neutral/N/A), or -1 (unfavorable). Write the values into `ai_signals`.\n183\t\n184\t| # | Signal | Frontmatter key | +1 Condition | -1 Condition |\n185\t|---|--------|----------------|-------------|-------------|\n186\t| 1 | Change specificity | `change_specificity` | Exact file paths, API endpoints, field names known | Vague scope (\"improve X\") |\n187\t| 2 | Pattern precedent | `pattern_precedent` | Similar changes exist in same codebase | No precedent in codebase |\n188\t| 3 | Adapter/plugin pattern | `adapter_pattern` | Follows existing reference implementation | N/A (0 if absent) |\n189\t| 4 | Existing foundation | `existing_foundation` | Extending existing code/feature | Greenfield, no foundation |\n190\t| 5 | Open questions | `open_questions` | All design decisions resolved for this epic | Open questions that would change implementation approach |\n191\t| 6 | External dependency | `external_dependency` | None | Upstream contribution or vendor coordination needed |\n192\t| 7 | Human process gates | `human_process_gates` | None | Requires human approval step |\n193\t| 8 | Repo access | `repo_access` | AI can clone and modify target repo | Repo inaccessible or special access required |\n194\t| 9 | Architecture claims | `architecture_claims` | Epic's scope or the strategy's premise about the component (surfaces, repos, deployment model, maturity state such as Tech Preview/GA) is corroborated by an architecture-context file — name that file in the rationale | Strategy asserts architecture that the context files contradict or cannot back |\n195\t\n196\t**Scoring `architecture_claims` (signal 9):** a strategy makes architecture claims whenever it states what a component IS — its maturity state (\"shipped as Tech Preview\", \"generally available\"), its CRD/API/repo surfaces, its deployment model — even when it never uses the word \"claim\". If the strategy indicates the resolution could require a different approach (conditional ADRs, \"if X requires changes to Y\"), evaluate which downstream epics build on the current assumption and gate them on the resolution.\n230\t\n231\t## Step 7: Derive Acceptance Criteria\n232\t\n233\tEach epic gets acceptance criteria derived from:\n234\t- Strategy acceptance criteria allocated to this epic's scope\n235\t- HLRs mapped to this epic\n236\t- Implementation-specific requirements (build pipeline green, rollback plan, doc review, etc.)\n237\t- Rules 23-25 from Step 5\n238\t\n239\tEvery AC must be a testable pass/fail condition on THIS epic's own deliverable — something the epic's engineering work produces or verifies. Set frontmatter via script:\n258\t\n259\t```bash\n260\tpython3 scripts/frontmatter.py set artifacts/epic-tasks/{ID}-decomposition.md \\\n261\t    parent_strat=\"{ID}\" epic_count=<N> critical_path_length=<N>\n262\t```\n263\t\n264\tAdd `triage=<value> triage_rationale=\"<reason>\"` for triaged strategies (Step 0).\n265\t\n266\t### Scope constraint: decompose, don't design\n267\t\n268\tYour job is to break strategy scope into units of work, not to make implementation decisions.\n269\tIf the strategy describes a capability at a functional level, the epic scope stays at that level.\n270\tDo not invent API paths, URL schemas, response formats, environment variables, caching policies,\n271\tCRD field names, or other implementation details not stated in the strategy. Do not set it earlier: anything you write or edit after setting it may be reviewed in a partially written state.\n353\t\n354\t### Conditional decomposition (when applicable)\n355\t\n356\tIf an Investigation epic has ≤3 bounded outcomes that change downstream structure, write one file per branch epic using the `-BRANCH-<letter>-` filename convention:\n357\t\n358\t```\n359\t{ID}-E001.md                        # Shared epic (the Investigation that selects the branch)\n360\t{ID}-BRANCH-A-E003.md               # If outcome A\n361\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E003.md               # If outcome B\n362\t{ID}-BRANCH-B-E004.md               # Extra epic in branch B\n363\t```\n364\t\n365\t**Branch epics are not standalone Jira issues.** The pipeline attaches each branch's epics to the gating Investigation epic as a plan document; it does not create them as issues or wire Blocks links from them.
